page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.3xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance based on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor operating at 3.2 GHz, it offers 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The hardware allocation includes 24.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, along with a 25 MB L3 cache. The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Instruction extensions supported include AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

Benchmarking highlights average performance across multi-core processor tests, such as a Passmark CPU score of 11610.14 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5654.0. Cached memory read throughput is high at 620.37 GB/sec, though uncached memory write operations drop to 24.54 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom performance quartile for memory write operations. Single-core execution on stress-ng also registers in the lower 25th percentile at 1149.99. Mid-sized LLM text generation is constrained, achieving 6.95 tokens/sec on 7B parameter models.

The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU allocation delivers qualitative resource efficiency for CPU-heavy tasks that do not require high memory footprints or fast local scratch disks. Given its 4 Gbps network capacity and steady multi-core results in static web serving (9.12 GB/sec) and Redis SET execution (9.94 million ops/sec), ecs.c4.3xlarge is suitable for application web serving, software compilation, batch processing, and general multi-threaded compute workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor. Configured with 12 vCPUs across 6 physical cores with hyperthreading, 24.0 GB of RAM, and no integrated local storage or GPU accelerators, it provides a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network connectivity is delivered at a baseline speed of 4 Gbps. Multi-core performance metrics, such as Geekbench multi-core scores and Passmark CPU benchmarks, sit in the average performance tier, while stress-ng single-core execution and uncached memory write throughput register in the lower performance quartile. The instance exhibits efficient processing for multi-threaded applications and web serving workloads, though performance drops under memory-write heavy or large LLM inference tasks. Overall, ecs.c4.3xlarge offers a balanced resource layout for moderate compute jobs, compilation tasks, and general web infrastructure without local disk dependencies.
